name: CapCut Pendulum Transition Movement
use_when: A high-energy CapCut, AMV, game, sports, or action clip feels too static before a transition.
The editor wants a strong swing or wobble layer after the clip timing is already beat-matched.
The next transition pass needs more physical movement without rebuilding the whole shot.
A stylized documentary cutout collage needs very subtle ambient drift after all text, cutouts, and evidence are already readable.
avoid_when: The pendulum movement makes the action pose, face, caption, product, or proof unreadable.
The clip already has enough shake, turbulence, wide-angle distortion, or graph zoom motion.
The project tone is calm, documentary, premium brand, or speech-led and swing motion would feel cheap.
The documentary scene contains dense evidence, source text, maps, or captions that would become harder to inspect.

timeline_pattern.pattern: locked_clip -> apply_pendulum -> preview_readability -> optional_second_pendulum -> optional_third_only_if_readable -> export_or_reimport -> transition_pass -> sfx_on_motion_peak
timeline_pattern.order_rule: Apply pendulum only after the clip is speed-matched and before the final transition/SFX review.
timeline_pattern.intensity_rule: One pendulum layer adds movement, two creates strong movement, and a third should be treated as an extreme style choice.
timeline_pattern.transition_rule: Judge pendulum strength together with the later transition effect because swing plus turbulence can quickly become unreadable.
timeline_pattern.documentary_texture_rule: For documentary collage use, treat Pendulum as low-strength texture rather than transition impact, and remove it if it competes with proof or typography.

motion.rule: Pendulum movement should add energy while the subject remains identifiable and the next cut remains readable.

keyframe_values.default_layers: Start with one pendulum pass; use two only when the style needs obvious swing.
keyframe_values.extreme_layers: Use three pendulum passes only after phone-size readability passes.
keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: The strongest swing, shake, or transition peak should land within 1-2 frames of the intended beat when sync matters.
keyframe_values.subtle_documentary_start: For subtle CapCut documentary texture, test Play Pendulum around speed 2, strength 3, twist 0, sharpen 0 after the scene already reads.

sound.rule: Use a whoosh, hit, or low swing accent only on the strongest visible motion peak, not on every wobble.

captions.rule: Move or suppress captions during the strongest swing if the movement makes text harder to read.

color.rule: No direct color rule; check that motion blur, glow, or compression from stacked movement does not muddy the frame.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate with short rotate/translate oscillation curves, optional motion blur, and contact-sheet checks around the swing peak.
implementation.remotion: Represent pendulum as a damped rotation/translation function with layerCount, peakFrame, amplitude, decay, and readability flags.
implementation.blender: Use a short camera or plane rotation/translation oscillation around the cut, then review motion blur and framing.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Apply the Pendulum effect to the locked clip, preview it, add a second Pendulum only if more movement is needed, and reserve a third for extreme edits that still read clearly.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Transform rotation/position keyframes or a preset wobble on an adjustment layer, then tune intensity after viewing it with adjacent clips.

common_mistakes: Adding pendulum before the clip is beat-matched.
Stacking multiple pendulums because the preset is available rather than because the transition needs it.
Letting swing motion hide the action pose or character face.
Forgetting to recheck captions and SFX after the movement changes perceived timing.
Using the same pendulum intensity on every clip until the edit feels mechanical.
Using documentary Pendulum drift on evidence-heavy screens where the viewer needs stillness.
qc: Does the pendulum movement have a named energy or transition job?
Is the action still readable at phone size after all pendulum layers?
Does the strongest swing land on the intended beat or transition peak?
Are captions clear or suppressed during the most unstable frames?
Does the motion still work when viewed with the following transition and SFX?
If used as documentary texture, does it remain subtle enough that titles, captions, cutouts, and proof stay readable?
